title: This is the story of how one million humans build a hundred times better way of living

source.note: Maia City play, the trailer every film linked; its version 31 of 2026-11-05

clips.camera: the one continuous drone take: over the mountain crest past the old tree, out of black, the whole city and the river below
clips.description: The fly-over starts under a huge old tree on the crest of a mountain at the city's edge, the low sun breaking through it; below, the nearest village: its tower at the centre and the master dome beside it, smaller, the large domes round them, stone paths, the river with a footbridge; more villages, each round its tower, in the morning mist toward the mountains.

clips.camera: the same take: over the crest's edge, one smooth descent over the city and the river down to the treetops of the food forest
clips.description: Low over the busy heart of a village: a wide stone plaza along the river full of people, a market under a dome's arcade, and beyond them the village's tower beside the great master dome, a third wider at its foot and two and a half times as tall. No cars.

clips.camera: the same take: low across the ring terrace of a dome (the flat top of its stone arcade, a living room open to the sky), then through a round stone arch
clips.description: Samuel walks away from us along a flagstone path through a round limestone arch toward the great master dome, alone in the arch in the morning haze; the one arch shot of the film.

clips.camera: the same take: inside, by the spring, Samuel walking toward us on a dry stone path, then close on his face gazing slightly upward
clips.description: Samuel's face in warm rim light, looking up at something huge with quiet wonder and a small smile; the dome's lattice and the forest soft behind him.

clips.camera: the take carries straight on from shot 4: Samuel lifts his face up into the camera and opens his arms wide; the camera begins to rise straight up
clips.description: Inside the great master dome: Samuel walks toward us through the food forest under the glass lattice, people eating together at long wooden tables beside a stream; beyond the glass, outside, the village tower rises over the gallery.

clips.camera: the same take: a vertical crane straight up, looking down through the dome's round opening at Samuel in the middle, looking up into the lens with his arms wide
clips.description: From the forest floor straight up a village's tower: its ring of limestone arches, its great glass foot rising like a dome and sweeping up into its tapering body and broad round crown, the sun flaring past its edge.

clips.camera: cut on "First in a game": a fast drone flight over the game's world map, deep low-poly jungle between the villages, that morphs in the same flight into the real city: glass domes on stone arcades in a jungle of a food forest, the glass bell towers, sun flares from the low sun, then the blue hour; the lights come on in every dome and the flight goes on at full speed over them, blending to black 2 s after the lights came on
clips.description: Over Samuel's shoulder: the master dome as it is in the game on his glass tablet, a single clear pane, and the real one in the same place behind it, its village's tower beside it, plainly bigger.

cues.text: This is the story of how

clips.line: This is the story of how one million humans build a hundred times better way of living. Our own solarpunk city, from the ground up.
First in a game, then for real.

clips.pace: Music-locked montage, 1.5–2 s cuts, speeding up
clips.sound: The trailer, the same in every film (its own story): Samuel's "This is the story..." in a breath of soft open air, its own theme (cinematic, hopeful, friendly; D major, about 105 bpm) swelling in under "...of how one million humans" and rising through the line, held back under "First in a game, then for real.", its big chord right after "real." and ringing out under "Maia, can you..."
clips.camera: Montage: IN THE GAME (teal) and FOR REAL (gold), Samuel montaged into the real city; on screen "100x" alone and large while he says "a hundred times"
